profile: A history reader interested in the Industrial Revolution, the Roman Empire and the history of science.

shelf.title: The Steam Engine and the Age of Machines
shelf.gist: Explains how the steam engine, refined over decades, freed factories from rivers and became the mechanical heart of the industrial revolution.

shelf.title: Cotton Mills of Lancashire
shelf.gist: An essay on how the cotton mills of Lancashire depended on child labour and reshaped whole towns around the rhythm of the machine.

shelf.title: Children of the Factory Floor
shelf.gist: A news-style report on child labour in the industrial revolution's cotton mills, and the campaign that finally brought railways of inspectors and reformers to the factory gates.

shelf.title: Iron Rails, Iron Will: Building Britain's Railways
shelf.gist: A blog post celebrating how railways, powered by the steam engine, replaced the horse and stitched the country together faster than anyone expected.

shelf.title: The Roman Legions on the March
shelf.gist: An essay on how the discipline of the Roman legions, more than any single general, held the Roman Empire together for centuries.

shelf.title: Roads That Built an Empire
shelf.gist: An explainer on how the Roman Empire's road network, engineered to outlast the men who built it, bound distant provinces of the Roman Empire together.

shelf.title: The Fall of Rome, Revisited
shelf.gist: An essay reconsidering why the Roman Empire's legions, once unbeatable, could no longer hold the frontier by the empire's final morning.

shelf.title: Hadrian's Wall: The Empire's Northern Edge
shelf.gist: A blog post on Hadrian's Wall as the visible edge of the Roman Empire, patrolled by legions who traded the horse for a life on foot along the frontier.

shelf.title: The Royal Society and the Birth of Modern Science
shelf.gist: An explainer on how the Royal Society turned scattered curiosity into a shared method, corresponding by letter about experiments including Darwin's later work on natural selection.

shelf.title: Newton's Quiet Revolution
shelf.gist: An essay on how Isaac Newton, working largely alone, used the Royal Society and the printing press to turn private calculation into shared, lasting science.

shelf.title: Darwin's Voyage and the Idea of Natural Selection
shelf.gist: A news-style account of how Charles Darwin's voyage supplied the evidence behind natural selection, which he later brought before the Royal Society and set in print by the printing press.

shelf.title: The Printing Press and the Spread of Ideas
shelf.gist: An essay on how the printing press turned the rare, hand-copied book into an ordinary object, letting the Royal Society and ideas like natural selection reach a wide public.

shelf.title: Threads of Change: Cotton, Steam and the Factory Age
shelf.gist: A blog post tying together the steam engine, the railways and the cotton mills of the industrial revolution, and the child labour that powered all three.
